## Product-source drift

Fresh GitHub Releases identify AgentSight `v1.0.25`, published 16 August 2026 from product commit `0080545f7c6b110ec2d4a4af5100b58f514c84d5`. The release contains product PR `#194`, **fix: preserve provider session messaging compatibility**.

The change is material runtime behavior rather than a version-only release:

- Codex transcript resume prefers the session's recorded standalone CLI version when usable while preserving the existing PATH fallback;
- provider initialization, resume, JSON-RPC, timeout, transport-close, and immediate process-exit failures propagate instead of being reported as false acceptance;
- one runtime lock is held per session, so concurrent submissions to the same session are rejected rather than interleaved;
- AgentSight does not automatically resend an ambiguously delivered message;
- Direct and relay preserve the public 65,536-byte decoded-message contract;
- Node relay work is bounded to eight local requests concurrently, while Controller keeps at most 64 pending browser requests per Node;
- provider work, Node relay, Controller, and browser paths use bounded deadlines rather than unbounded waits;
- Unix root execution drops to the transcript owner with a minimal non-secret environment; Windows provider execution is restricted to a non-elevated current-user context and canonical transcripts beneath the user's home directory.

The existing Product, Architecture, and Changelog canonicals already own the relevant reader decisions; no new v1.0.25 page was justified. The delivered rendered outcome updates release/source identity, explains the current messaging behavior in Changelog and `llms.txt`, and preserves all existing canonical ownership.
